title: Sell Mineral Rights in Taylorstown, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Taylorstown, PA
metaDescription: Own farmland minerals near Taylorstown, close to the WV line in Washington County? We buy Marcellus interests directly and pay cash.
heroLead: Taylorstown is about as rural as Washington County gets, tucked close to the West Virginia line, where working farms still outnumber housing developments and a family's mineral rights usually came down through the same land they still farm today.
intro: Taylorstown is a small unincorporated community in Washington County, near the West Virginia border, in an area that's remained largely agricultural even as gas development has reshaped much of the rest of the county. Farms here have often stayed in the same family for generations, which usually means cleaner title history than areas with a lot of turnover, but it also means mineral rights sometimes haven't been reviewed since the original lease was signed during the boom years.

Washington County is the heart of the wet-gas Marcellus play, and operators have steadily worked their way through rural townships like the one surrounding Taylorstown, pooling farm acreage into units over the years.

sections.heading: Farmland That's Stayed in the Family
paragraphs: If your family has farmed the same ground near Taylorstown for generations, your title is often more straightforward than what we see in more developed parts of the county. That said, an original lease signed fifteen or more years ago is worth pulling out and reading again, especially the post-production deduction language.

sections.heading: Being Near the State Line Doesn't Change the Rules
paragraphs: Because Taylorstown sits so close to West Virginia, we sometimes hear from families who assume different rules apply here than elsewhere in Pennsylvania. They don't. Any mineral interest physically located in Washington County falls under Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act and the state's specific case law on deductions, regardless of how close the state line sits.

faqs.question: Does being near West Virginia change how my mineral rights are governed?
faqs.answer: No. Any interest located in Washington County, Pennsylvania is governed entirely by Pennsylvania law, regardless of proximity to the state line.

faqs.question: My family has farmed this land for generations. Is the title simple to confirm?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, but we still verify the full chain of title and confirm the current generation's ownership is properly recorded before making an offer.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling in this rural part of the county?
faqs.answer: Development has steadily expanded into rural Washington County townships over the years. We check current DEP records against your specific tract to confirm what applies to you.

faqs.question: Should I talk to a tax advisor before selling farmland mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It's worth a conversation, especially if the interest was part of a larger inherited farm. We aren't tax advisors ourselves, but we're glad to work alongside your CPA or attorney during the process.
